raw.body:
React Compiler currently compiles components/hooks wrapped in MobX `observer` (e.g. from `mobx-react` or `mobx-react-lite`) silently because they look like normal React functional components. However, MobX relies on executing the component function in a tracking context during render. By caching/memoizing the JSX output of the component without tracing MobX observable dependencies, the React Compiler breaks MobX reactivity, causing components to render stale data.

This change updates `getReactFunctionType` in the Compiler Entrypoint (`Program.ts`) to check if a function is wrapped by MobX's `observer` (either directly inline or via variable/identifier references). If so, it bails out of compilation and returns `null`, keeping the component reactive.

## How did you test this change?

Added a compiler fixture test `skip-mobx-observer.js` to ensure the compiler bails out when detecting a MobX observer wrapper.
raw.title: [Compiler] Skip compiling components/hooks wrapped in MobX observer HOC
